newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka economy to grow 5.5 pct in 1997 - broker.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka economy to grow 5.5 pct in 1997 - broker.

text.p: The Sri Lankan economy should stage a strong recovery in 1997 led by growth in industry, a report by brokerage CT Smith said.
The report, received by Reuters on Friday, said:
"The overall recovery in key sectors -- against low bases of 1996 -- will enable the economy to grow 5.5 percent in 1997.
The forecast contrasts with the latest prediction of the Central Bank, which expects Sri Lankan gross domestic product (GDP) growth of at least six percent this year.

Sri Lankan GDP fell to 3.8 percent in 1996, from 5.5 percent in 1995, due mainly to a severe drought, which led to power cuts of five hours a day from March to August and hit industry and agriculture.
"The absence of an energy crisis as in 1996 will result in improved performance from the industrial sector, which is expected to post growth in excess in 10 percent," the report said.
The report also said the service sector should grow by about six percent in 1997 compared to 5.7 in 1996, due mainly to an overall improvement in the economic climate.
Agriculture would post a modest recovery and grow by one percent in 1997, compared to a contraction of 4.6 percent last year, the report said.
